transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. Like, I’ll be trying to fix a rendering bug at work, and then a Slack ping or some color pattern on the screen—or even a siren outside—pulls me off into a completely different idea before I finish the line of code. It’s making it really hard to get anything done.
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being like this when I was a kid, at least not in a way that stood out. I got through school okay, but I’d have to think more about it.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or wired compared with your normal self?

Yeah. Lately I’ve felt really wired, like there’s this current running through me all the time. I wake up already thinking about features I want to build, layouts for an exhibition, press angles, code changes—just a whole list of things. Sitting still feels like I’m wasting the moment.
When you feel wired like that, do you need less sleep than usual?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t been paying close attention to the exact hours. I feel wired when I’m up, but I don’t know if I’m actually sleeping less than usual or just not noticing it.
Does this trouble focusing mostly happen during the times when you feel unusually wired?

Yeah, mostly then. When I’m wired, it’s like I can’t keep my mind on one thing. I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping or some color pattern or even a siren outside sends me off into a whole different idea before I finish what I was doing.
When you feel wired like that, do you also feel more confident or powerful than usual?

Yeah… I do. I feel like I can see connections other people are missing. Like I’m the only one who can really bring together generative art, Mexican visual traditions, and the tech community in a way that could change how people in the city think about public art.
During these wired periods, do you feel more important or more gifted than other people?

Yeah… during those times I do feel like I’m more gifted, I guess. Like I’m the only person who can connect generative art, Mexican visual traditions, and the tech community in a way that could actually change how the city sees public art.
When you feel wired like that, do you start taking on a lot more projects or activities than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I start taking on way more than I normally would. I’ll be emailing curators, pitching ideas to community leaders, rewriting parts of the backend, sketching out installation plans, and trying to pull other developers in… sometimes at all hours. It starts feeling bigger than my regular job, like I have to keep pushing it forward.
During these wired periods, do you find yourself talking much more than usual?

Yeah. I talk a lot more. Once I start explaining the platform, I just keep going—how the architecture works, the funding angle, the cultural impact, the deployment plan. People have told me they can’t really get a word in. At the time it doesn’t feel strange to me, it feels like the thoughts are coming too fast to stop.
During these wired periods, do your thoughts ever race so fast that they’re hard to keep up with?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I can tell my mind is moving fast, but I don’t know if I’d describe it as so fast I can’t keep up. It’s more like there are a lot of ideas at once, and I’m trying to follow them.
During these wired periods, do you feel driven to start or push forward a lot of projects or plans?

Yes. I get really driven to move things forward. I’ll be emailing curators, pitching community leaders, rewriting parts of the backend, planning out installations, trying to recruit other developers… and it can be at all hours. It starts feeling like the project is bigger than my regular job, like I have to keep pushing it.
When you feel wired like that, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve tracked it closely. I might stay up later when I’m wired, but I can’t say for sure that I need a lot less sleep.
During these wired periods, do you feel unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah… most days during those times I do feel kind of lit up. Like everything is finally clicking, like Glendale is finally catching up to what I’ve been building. It can feel like I’m unstoppable.

But it’s not just happy. I also get really irritated if my wife or people at work slow me down with what they call “process.” I can snap pretty hard when that happens.
What’s the longest these wired periods have lasted without letting up?
Probably about three months now. It really started when my platform got picked for the Glendale showcase, and it hasn’t fully let up since then.
During this wired period, have you been hospitalized for your mood or behavior?
I’m not sure how to answer that. I haven’t been keeping track of it that way, and I don’t think I have anything specific to point to.
During this wired period, has it caused serious problems at work or at home?

Yeah. I mean, I guess I have to admit it has.

Work put me on leave after I went around the normal approval process and pushed changes myself. I thought it needed to happen, but they saw it as a big problem.

And at home… my wife says the spending and the arguments have made everything feel unstable. So yes, it’s definitely caused problems.
During this wired period, have you heard or seen things that other people said were not there?
I don’t think so. I haven’t been seeing things or hearing voices that other people said weren’t there. At least, nothing like that comes to mind.
